### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**12** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 434c6c7cab6aee9c5587e680d7eeeb445a756714` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ab0aa4e7e151aa4b51e194d94d0736f66510d945` — the merge of head `dd39cf5405645b240b36b7aba5f35bdfc66b20cd` into base `434c6c7cab6aee9c5587e680d7eeeb445a756714`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ab0aa4e7e151aa4b51e194d94d0736f66510d945 && git checkout ab0aa4e7e151aa4b51e194d94d0736f66510d945
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 434c6c7cab6aee9c5587e680d7eeeb445a756714 dd39cf5405645b240b36b7aba5f35bdfc66b20cd && git checkout -B drift-repro 434c6c7cab6aee9c5587e680d7eeeb445a756714 && git merge --no-ff dd39cf5405645b240b36b7aba5f35bdfc66b20cd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 434c6c7cab6aee9c5587e680d7eeeb445a756714
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dd39cf5405645b240b36b7aba5f35bdfc66b20cd`
Local-runs: none

PR #21258 for card #21216. The head is the tip of `claude/issue-21216-action-translation-keyed-children` (fetched, sha confirmed); the net diff reviewed is `origin/main...` that ref: 3 files, +604/-22. Inputs: the card body and all five comments (`5937261840` triage, `5939443403` unlock, `5941298378` claim, `5942505415` dev report, `5942526356` seat answer), the PR body and file list, and the head's check-runs. Read-only throughout: declared sets and read sites were verified on `origin/main` with `git show`, and the sibling at the `.objectui-sha` pin `31971ff1`. Rendered 2026-10-01T23:35Z.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged against the triage direction (`5937261840`) and the runtime read sites:

1. `outcomeMessages.OUTCOME` under `_actions.ACTION` and `globalActions.ACTION`, judged against the keys of the action's own `outcomeMessages`, `translation-target-unknown` at error — RIGHT. `resolveActionOutcomeMessages` (`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`) iterates `Object.keys(action.outcomeMessages)` and returns `undefined` before any bundle read when the action declares none; `translateAction` is its only caller; no other reader of these bundle keys exists in this repo (`packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts` is a producer) or in objectui at the pin (zero hits). So every outcome key on an action without `outcomeMessages` is unread, and refusing each one is sound. Code and level are `params`' own, as the direction asked; no second vocabulary.
2. `resultDialog.fields.PATH`, judged against the literal `resultDialog.fields[].path`, same code and level — RIGHT. `resolveActionResultDialog` returns `action.resultDialog` untouched when it is absent (nothing read), maps only the declared `fields[]` by `path`, and reads no label when `fields` is omitted (`ActionSchema.resultDialog.fields` is optional, described "Omit to dump full JSON", so the finding's JSON sentence is TRUE). objectui `useObjectLabel.actionResultDialog` returns `spec` when it is undefined and indexes the fetched `fields` node by the literal path. The gap was real on `main`: the action walk there has exactly one leg (`checkActionParams`), which is consistent with the dev's door probe at `be5a83cf`. A dotted path is one member; `memberPath` brackets it, matching how both resolvers index.
3. `params.NAME.options.VALUE`, judged against a declared param's inline `options[].value` as `String(value)`, `translation-option-key-unknown` at warning with the label-versus-value diagnosis — RIGHT, and it belongs to this family: an option map is a record keyed by a declared name. `translateActionParams` overlays `String(opt.value)` over the inline array and nothing else. Field-backed params with no inline options are left unjudged by design — CORRECT and necessary: objectui's `useConsoleActionRuntime` runs `resolveActionParams` (field inheritance) and then `actionParamOptionLabel` over the resolved `p.options`, so those bundle keys ARE read in the console; refusing them would be a false positive, and judging them would re-derive the inheritance inside lint. The no-options-and-no-field map warns once, mirroring `checkOptionKeys`' "declares no options" branch. Severity: the seat's answer A (`5942526356`) is right — the module's Severity note (ADR-0072 D1) keeps the option shape at warning and the field leg is the one vocabulary for it; B would judge one key shape two ways.
4. Reach of the new legs — RIGHT: they run only after the action key resolved at its address. A bound action under `globalActions` and an object-less action under `_actions` still take the orphan `continue`, so the new legs add no new disagreement with the resolvers (③, class b).
5. `localePath` through `memberPath` — output byte-identical (identifier → `.locale`, otherwise `["locale"]`). RIGHT.
6. Public surface of `@objectstack/lint` — exports unchanged (`validateTranslationReferences`, the two rule ids, `TranslationRefFinding`); `ActionEntryContext` is module-private. No `packages/spec` file is touched, so no regenerated artifact is owed. The accept-set that moves is the authoring door's: three key shapes, two at error, one at warning. RIGHT.
7. The coverage pin — a TEST, not a new gate. It is an `it` block inside the existing suite, the twin of the #13835 object-branch pin in the same file; it adds no check script, CI job, hook, patrol row or ratchet, and `dispatch-gates` derives no new family from it. 「新增门禁默认否」 governs gates; a pin inside an existing test family is ordinary test work, and the pin reads the spec shape through the `@objectstack/spec/system` dependency edge the #13835 pin already uses. Its ledger matches the schema on `main`: 15 keys (`label`, `description`, `confirmText`, `successMessage`, `outcomeMessages`, `params`, `params.*.label`, `params.*.helpText`, `params.*.placeholder`, `params.*.options`, `resultDialog`, `resultDialog.title`, `resultDialog.description`, `resultDialog.acknowledge`, `resultDialog.fields`), and `globalActions` is built by the same `actionTranslationSchema` factory, so the bound-equals-global assertion holds. Its new `container` kind is where ③ class c sits.
8. Census, re-read at the code — RIGHT. `@objectstack/platform-objects` generated bundles: 16 `resultDialog.fields` keys per locale (`user.email`, `user.phoneNumber`, `temporaryPassword` twice, `totpURI` twice, `backupCodes` four times, `client.client_id`, `client.client_secret`, `client_secret`, `dnsRecordType`, `dnsRecordName`, `dnsRecordValue`), each matching a declared `path` on `sys_user`, `sys_two_factor`, `sys_oauth_application` or `sys_sso_provider`, 64 over four locales; 11 param-option keys per locale (`link_social.provider` 7, `create_oauth_application.type` 4), all declared inline, 44 over four locales; 0 outcome keys. `app-showcase`'s action entries carry `label`, `successMessage` and param `label`/`helpText` only; `app-crm`, `app-todo` and `app-multi-package` ship no action translation entry. Nothing published is newly refused.

Finding messages, each sentence TRUE against the read sites: "Only the outcomes the action declares are translated, so this copy is never shown" (the resolver's loop); "declares no `outcomeMessages` at all, so nothing reads this map" (the early return); "declares no `resultDialog`, so nothing reads this label" (`if (!spec) return spec`); "it renders the whole response as JSON" (the schema's describe); "The resolver looks the option up by value" (`String(opt.value)` here, `o.value` in objectui).

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/21216-action-translation-keyed-children.md`: `'@objectstack/lint': minor`, body carrying `Clause-②: yes` with no arm — the same declaration as the PR body and the claim. RIGHT. `@objectstack/lint` 17.5.0 is a published package; the diff adds no export and removes none; what moves is that the authoring door refuses more. House precedent for exactly this shape: #21204 (card #21131, the options sibling, `unconsumed-widget-option`) shipped `minor` with `Clause-②: yes`; the #20553 door refusal is `minor`; #16310's promotion of this very rule to error sits under 17.5.0's Minor Changes. Not `(narrowing)`: no published schema or API accepts less — `TranslationDataSchema` still parses the key, the lint judges it. Not `skip-changeset`. `Check Changeset` on the head: success. No ADR-0087 marker is owed (not breaking).

Changeset prose, sentence by sentence: "`os validate`, `os build` and `os lint` now check…" TRUE (the rule runs inside `reference-integrity-suite`, which `runAuthoringRules` executes in `validate.ts`, in `compile.ts` which `build.ts` wraps, and in `lint.ts`); "Before this, only `params.NAME` was checked" TRUE; "the same code and level an undeclared `params` key already gets" TRUE; "`translateAction` overlays only the outcomes the action declares" TRUE; "The label lookup is keyed by each declared field's `path`, dots included" TRUE; the bracketed config path TRUE (`memberPath`); "the code and level a field's `options` key already gets" TRUE; "names the stored value when the key is a display label" TRUE; "warned once, because nothing reads it" TRUE; the field-backed inheritance sentence TRUE (objectui `resolveActionParams`, then `actionParamOptionLabel`); "fails `os validate` with exit 1 … `os build` refuses it" TRUE (error-severity authoring findings exit 1 in `validate.ts` and `compile.ts`); "The option-key warning changes an exit code only under `--strict`" TRUE for `os validate` (the final exit is 1 only when `flags.strict` is set and the warnings list is non-empty, otherwise 0) and `os lint` (`--strict`: fail on warning-severity findings too); the examples-and-platform-objects sentence TRUE (census, ① item 8).

PR-body prose: the table and the four "where the declared sets come from" bullets match the code; "`localePath` … byte-identical" TRUE. The `Tests`, `Reverse verification` and `Gates` sections are the dev's own runs and are not re-run here; the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts (③).

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (`5942505415`), each answered:

1. Options leg at `translation-option-key-unknown`/warning against the claim's literal `translation-target-unknown` — raised as open question 1; the seat answered A (`5942526356`); concur (① item 3). Closed.
2. Not merged with `origin/main` — now 6 commits behind (`434c6c7c`; 4 at report time). None of the six touches the three edited files, `i18n-resolver.ts`, `translation.zod.ts` or `action.zod.ts`; the only upstream `packages/lint` change is `validate-preset-comparands.*` in `3dc33b2d`; the PR reads `mergeable: true`. The declared sets the legs judge against are unchanged upstream. Accepted; the merge group re-judges the merged tree.
3. Lint suite and typecheck at `ac847edd`, head adds only the changeset — verified: `git diff --stat ac847edd dd39cf54` is the one changeset file. Closed.
4. ESLint narrowed to the two edited files — the head's `Lint & Repo Gates` check-run is the authority, and it concluded success (below). Closed.
5. No labels written; `needs:contract-review` is not on the PR (labels: documentation, size/l, tests, tooling), so nothing is owed on PASS. Closed.
6. Worktree cleanup — not visible in the diff; no finding.

Open question 1 — answered by the seat; closed as above.

Out-of-scope findings:

- Class b (a bound action filed under `globalActions`): CONFIRMED pre-existing at the code. On `main`, `lookupActionField`, `lookupActionResultDialogNode`, `lookupActionParamNode` and `resolveActionOutcomeMessages` all fall back to `globalActions.ACTION` for a BOUND action on an object-scoped miss, and objectui `actionSuffixes` documents the same fallback, while the lint's orphan text says "never read" and its pin ("tells an object-bound action filed under globalActions where it belongs") predates this PR; the `translation.zod.ts` docblock sides with the lint ("object-less"). This PR touches neither side and reaches no new leg there. ESCALATED to the seat as its own card: which side moves is a contract-first ruling, not a dev's call. Not a defect of this PR.
- Class c (`resultDialog.title`, `description`, `acknowledge` on an action that declares no `resultDialog`): CONFIRMED unread — `resolveActionResultDialog` returns `spec` (undefined) and objectui `actionResultDialog` returns `spec` when it is undefined. May this PR leave it out? YES. The card's closeout clause is "one walk judges every KEYED child of an action's translation entry against its declaration"; these three are leaf prose under a fixed key, not a record keyed by a declared name, and the pin states the classification (`resultDialog` container, its leaves leaf-copy) instead of burying it. But it is a class (c) authoring trap with reach measured at the door, and this PR closes the family card, so "named into #21216's family, not a point card" would leave it with no carrier. ESCALATED: the seat files a card for it; the triage's no-point-card bar covered the keyed-children positions only. The natural shape is one leg refusing the whole `resultDialog` node when the action declares none, beside the `fields` message that already says "declares no `resultDialog`".

Docs, outside this review's gate (prose is the seat's ACCEPT, per contract-review.md) and noted for it: the rule table in `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx` has no row for the three new key shapes, and `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` enumerates the refused kinds without "outcome" and "result field". Neither sentence is false; both are now incomplete. The claim's file surface named only generated rule-docs pages, and these are hand-written; `skills/**` is Tier H. A follow-up, not a FAIL.

Check-runs on `dd39cf54`, read at 2026-10-01T23:34Z: 34 check runs, 31 `success` and 3 `skipped` (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, each skipped by its own path filter), 0 failed, 0 in progress. The last to conclude were `Lint & Repo Gates` (23:28Z), `Type Check · workspace` and `TypeScript Type Check` (23:28Z), and the six `Test Core` shards with their rollup (23:23Z to 23:34Z); `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI` and `Temporal Conformance` are success.
